summary: The IDF is conducting airstrikes on Nabatieh and Ali Taher in southern Lebanon while simultaneously launching large-scale multi-front drills in Eilat and the north. Iran and the US are exchanging accusations over the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran declaring a new restricted zone and the US denying Iranian claims of attacking a SENTINEL drone. Hezbollah reportedly received Iranian approval to withdraw from Ali Taher ridge.

sections.executive_summary: The IDF is simultaneously conducting airstrikes on Nabatieh and Ali Taher in southern Lebanon while launching large-scale multi-front drills testing scenarios across Lebanon, the West Bank, and Gaza. Iran and the US are exchanging accusations over the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran declaring a new restricted zone and the IRGC claiming to have attacked a US drone. Hezbollah reportedly received Iranian approval to withdraw from Ali Taher ridge, signaling potential shifts in the Lebanon front.
iran: Iran's IRGC claimed on Sunday 15 Shahrivar to have targeted an unmanned SENTINEL drone in the Strait of Hormuz, but US Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesperson Captain Hawkins called the claim a 'pure lie' (Source: @VahidOnline/78257).

Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary announced a new restricted zone beyond the Strait of Hormuz will be declared in coming days, warning that any vessel entering without coordination with Tehran will be placed on an Iranian sanctions list (Source: @presstv/205777).

Iran's government raised the third-tier gasoline price to 10,000 tomans per liter starting 17 Shahrivar, while maintaining the monthly quota of 60 liters at 1,500 tomans and 50 liters at 3,000 tomans (Source: @VahidOnline/78258).

US Treasury Secretary stated that combined naval embargo and broad US sanctions have severely limited Tehran's ability to sell oil, estimating only approximately 30 million barrels of Iranian crude remain unsold by China (Source: @mamlekate/104344).

Former US Defense Secretary Leon Panetta warned that the 'Iran war' will likely continue at least six more months and could become an 'endless war' similar to Iraq and Afghanistan (Source: @mamlekate/104351).

Iranian Brigadier General claimed the Strait of Hormuz was open until February 28 when Israel attacked Iran, accusing Washington of waging an illegitimate war and disrupting commercial navigation (Source: @naya_foriraq/89499).
Iranian security forces clashed with terrorist elements in Zahedan, southeast Iran, with an initial toll of 2 killed (Source: @naya_foriraq/89498).
israel: IDF and Israel Police announced a large-scale pre-planned drill in Eilat and the Arava led by Division 80, practicing complex extreme scenarios in air, sea, and land with emphasis on protecting communities (Source: @New_security8200/203640).

IDF launched a snap drill under Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir testing simultaneous multi-front crises including 10-15 terrorists infiltrating from Lebanon, Route 60 attack in West Bank, Tel Aviv rocket attacks, and Yellow Line fighting in Gaza; the IDF shifted to a defensive posture on all fronts (Source: @manniefabian/59109).

IDF alerted northern residents that a series of attacks are expected in the coming hours on the Lebanon front, with explosions anticipated in the Valley of Hula, Ramim Ridge, and possibly northern Golan (Source: @pkpoi/143869).

Israeli intelligence assessments cited by the New York Post indicate Iran and its regional allies are increasing preparations for a coordinated surprise multi-domain attack on Israel (Source: @pkpoi/143862).

The Israeli government approved an expanded 'Shield of the North' project providing grants of up to 182,000 NIS for fortified rooms, covering approximately 11,000 housing units with a budget of approximately 4.2 billion NIS (Source: @almogboker78/18141).
IDF announced massive explosions expected in the northern Gaza envelope, Sha'ar HaNegev regional council, and the city of Sderot as part of ongoing operations (Source: @New_security8200/203654).
IDF struck a vehicle in central Gaza reportedly eliminating a Hamas military wing commander (Source: @yediotnews25/134723).

sections.threat_assessment: The convergence of active IDF airstrikes in Lebanon, a large-scale multi-front drill simulating simultaneous crises, and Iranian-US tensions over the Strait of Hormuz indicates an elevated threat environment across multiple theaters. Israeli intelligence assessments suggest Iran and its allies are preparing for a coordinated surprise attack, while Iran's declaration of a new restricted zone beyond the Strait of Hormuz and the IRGC's disputed claim of attacking a US drone raise the risk of miscalculation. Former Defense Secretary Panetta's warning that the conflict could extend at least six more months as an 'endless war' underscores the protracted nature of the current escalation.
sections.regional_response: Regional actors are responding to the escalating crisis through both military and economic measures. Saudi Arabia reports that Hezbollah has received Iranian approval to withdraw from Ali Taher ridge, suggesting possible de-escalation on the Lebanon front even as strikes continue. The US has denied Iranian claims of drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and is enforcing a naval embargo on Iranian oil, while Iran is countering with new restricted zones and sanctions threats. Iran's domestic response includes gasoline price increases and border trade disruptions, with approximately 23 devices at border crossings causing significant delays.
sections.intelligence_notes: The IDF's snap drill under Lt. Gen. Zamir deliberately excluded an Iranian ballistic missile scenario to avoid making the exercise artificially decisive, instead focusing on creating operational dilemmas for commanders across multiple fronts simultaneously. The drill tested scenarios including infiltration from Lebanon, West Bank attacks, Tel Aviv rocket strikes, and Gaza border breaches, with the entire military shifting to a defensive posture afterward. Israeli intelligence is specifically monitoring Iran's multi-domain preparations, while the disputed Strait of Hormuz incident between the IRGC and US CENTCOM requires verification before drawing conclusions about the actual threat level to maritime traffic.
